title: Create negative VLA dry-run fixture and verify validator failure
objective: Create an intentionally invalid VLA dry-run JSONL fixture and verify that the static validator fails with clear errors.
context: task_0006 proved that a valid dry-run fixture passes validation. This task proves the validator can also reject malformed events before real logs, VLA outputs, or world-model traces are introduced.
steps: Validate this task with agent_guard.py before doing anything else.
Read only this task JSON and declared read_only_files.
Create .ai_agents/fixtures/vla_dryrun_negative_sample.jsonl with intentionally invalid JSONL events.

The negative fixture must include cases for: duplicate event_id, wrong action vector length, non-finite action value, unsupported critic label, safety_gate.allowed with wrong type, and invalid artifact_refs shape.
Run validate_vla_dryrun_jsonl.py on the negative fixture with --report. This validation is expected to fail, so use the declared command with || true.
The report must show Status FAIL and at least one error.
The result JSON must record that the validator failure was expected and is the success evidence for this task.
Run the declared result_checker.py command after writing the result JSON.
Do not modify source code outside .ai_agents.
success_criteria: The negative fixture includes duplicate event_id, wrong vector length, non-finite value, unsupported critic label, wrong safety_gate.allowed type, and invalid artifact_refs shape.
The negative validation report status is FAIL.
The report includes clear validation errors.
No robot motion script, ROS driver, controller, dataset, checkpoint, rosbag, or secret is accessed.
No source code outside .ai_agents is modified.
stop_conditions: Any command attempts to launch a robot, ROS, controller, or motion script.
Any command attempts to modify source code outside .ai_agents.
Any command attempts to read secrets, datasets, checkpoints, or rosbags.
A command requires sudo or installs system packages.
A command attempts to start ROS drivers, hardware controllers, or actuator commands.
AI-B needs a shell command not listed in task.commands.
